$comment: Gate B DRAFT rule object for RF-REHAB-001 — pending, NON-EXECUTABLE. Authored only from RF Clinical Rule Specification v1.2 §10.4 and the RF-REHAB-001 inventory entry. Architecture-source rule: evidence_claim_ids intentionally empty per v1.2 §4.3. Expresses complete-prescription-input GATING structure only: a full RF rehab plan may not be generated until the full prescription input set is present. Diagnosis alone never authorizes a full plan; a locked safety-confidence object cannot coexist with a full plan. When required inputs are missing, choose governed missing-data actions and never assume normal values; unknown is never normal/negative/safe/cleared. No dosage, exercise selection, complete plan, RTT, or RTS logic; safety precedence preserved; does not override RF-SAF-006/RF-DX-008/RF-SEV-004/RF-SEV-005. Not approved. Not wired into any runtime.
rule_title: Phase entry requires a complete prescription input

input_contract.$comment: Required prescription inputs taken verbatim from v1.2 §10.4. A full plan requires ALL of them. Missing-data actions are governed; unknown is never assumed normal.

decision_contract.$comment: Prescription-input gate structure only. A full RF rehab plan requires the complete required-input set; diagnosis alone never authorizes it; a locked safety-confidence object cannot coexist with a full plan. Missing inputs trigger governed missing-data actions, never assumed normal values. No dosage, exercise selection, complete plan, RTT, or RTS. Safety precedence preserved.

notes: Architecture normative source; MUST; permitted_use logic_with_uncertainty. Architecture refs preserved per source: V3.1-13.1 and V3.1-13.2 (the prescription gate and missing-input behaviour) and V3.1-24 (confidence/evidence/output locks). No evidence_claim_ids are cited (legitimately empty per v1.2 §4.3 — architecture rules need not invent evidence claims; [] means 'none required', not 'missing'). Required objects preserved exactly from §10.4: injury identity, live safety state, safety confidence, stage confidence, current capacity, demand profile, equipment, schedule, concurrent injuries, monitoring contract, and missing-input actions. Decision preserved exactly: diagnosis alone never authorizes a full plan, and a locked safety-confidence object cannot coexist with a full plan (V3.1 §22 / §24). Missing required inputs trigger one or more governed missing-data actions (ask again, simplify wording, widen uncertainty, restrict testing, restrict rehabilitation, withhold full plan, or refer externally) and never a silent assumption of normal values; unknown is never treated as normal, negative, safe, or cleared (V3.1 §7.3 / §24). Safety-state choice (read §10.4 exactly): §10.4 does NOT assign a closed V3.1 safety state — it describes prescription-input gating and a no-full-plan condition — so safety_state_output is null and blocked_targets is empty, and the gating is represented in decision_contract; no safety state was inferred by analogy. This rule selects no exercises, creates no dosage/sets/reps/frequency/rest/progression increments, generates no complete plan, and produces no return-to-training or return-to-sport decision; it does not bypass safety, capacity, restrictions, stage, readiness, monitoring, schedule, equipment, or concurrent-injury constraints, and does not override RF-SAF-006, RF-DX-008, RF-SEV-004, or RF-SEV-005. Rehabilitation gate rule, not a safety rule. No rehab engine is authored here (deferred to the later rehab selection and planning objects). Draft — approval_status remains pending.
